pairing: PAIRING-1: the lag-arc as named signature

entries.authors: Wan WY, Wang J, Weatherburn DJ
entries.title: Does gambling expenditure have any effect on crime?
entries.key_finding: Panel ARDL (autoregressive distributed lag) explicitly decomposes expenditure-crime relationship into short-run vs long-run components. Method template exists but applied to gambling, not public spending.
entries.effect_size: short-run vs long-run elasticities reported in full text

entries.title: Does Economic Growth Reduce Crime? Evidence from India Using an ARDL Model
entries.key_finding: India 1995-2022 annual time series; ARDL bounding of short-run and long-run effects of government expenditure (among GFCF, inflation, rule of law) on crime.
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (lag structure applied to govt expenditure; country macro, not US city)

entries.authors: Chalfin A, Hansen B, Weisburst EK, Williams MC
entries.title: Police Force Size and Civilian Race
entries.key_finding: Each additional police officer abates ~0.1 homicides; per-capita effects twice as large for Black victims; level-elasticity of sworn-force size, no lag-arc timing
entries.effect_size: ~0.1 homicide per additional officer (national panel event-study)

entries.authors: Lund JJ, Schleimer JP, Reeping PM, Pear VA et al.
entries.title: Public funds, public safety (scoping review)
entries.key_finding: Of 33 spending-violence studies: 'All studies were ecologic, 24 were serial cross-sectional'; NO named lag-arc/timing taxonomy; timing treated as nuisance, not signature.

entries.title: Prosecutor politics: The impact of election cycles on criminal sentencing in the era of rising incarceration
entries.key_finding: Election-timing drives admissions (+3%, ~63,000 additional prison admissions 1986-2006): anticipatory timing effects exist in criminal-legal outputs - near-analog to anticipatory-spending mechanics.
entries.design: Panel DiD exploiting DA election timing, ~40 states

entries.authors: Guo X, Peng L, Shi X
entries.title: The Impact of Unemployment Insurance Benefit Cuts on Mental Health: Evidence From Early Pandemic Program Expirations
entries.key_finding: High-frequency Census Pulse DiD: timing of benefit termination moves anxiety outcomes - spending/benefit TIMING has measurable population effects (MH endpoint, not crime).
entries.effect_size: DiD on anxiety probability among non-college working-age adults

entries.authors: Basu S, Phillips R, Hoang H
entries.title: Impact of Community Health Center Losses on County-Level Mortality: A Natural Experiment in the United States, 2011-2019
entries.key_finding: PS-matched county DiD on CHC site losses (177 counties, 2014): infrastructure-loss shocks move mortality - design template for discretionary-spending shocks.
entries.effect_size: mortality effect estimates in full text

summary: Novelty verdict summary (PAIRING-1): Lagged structure of expenditure-outcome relationships is methodologically VERIFIED (panel ARDL short-run/long-run decompositions: Wan 2024 gambling-crime; Saigal & Gupta 2026 India govt-expenditure-crime) and adjacent causal timing effects exist (Chalfin 2022 officer elasticity; Okafor 2026 election-cycle admissions; Guo 2026 benefit-expiration timing). BUT: a NAMED 'lag-arc' signature - a systematic temporal response curve of violent crime to discretionary public-spending changes, characterized as a signature (e.g., effects peaking t-0..t-2) - was NOT found in any retrieved work. The anchor absence-evidence is Lund 2025: the whole spending-violence literature is ecologic, 24/33 serial cross-sectional, with no timing taxonomy. => the lag-arc as a named signature = NOVEL-ANGLE; the underlying lagged-effects phenomenon = VERIFIED/EXTENDED. Confidence in absence-search: medium (Crossref wall blocked the econ-literature sweep: NBER/RePEc econometrics of expenditure timing not fully covered by biomed routes).
source_routes: EuropePMC (resultType=core) + PubMed esearch/efetch; Crossref partial (first-pass only); OpenAlex + Semantic Scholar hard-429-walled
abstract_policy: Every entry's abstract loaded first-hand unless tagged secondhand; effect sizes only where stated in loaded abstract.
